name: ComfyUI
summary: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

agent_entrypoints.what: Installation, node reference, and the workflow model.
The local server's HTTP and WebSocket routes - what to POST to /prompt, and how to follow progress. Read before driving an instance programmatically.
Local HTTP API of a running ComfyUI instance. POST a workflow graph as JSON to generate images programmatically; poll /history/{prompt_id} for results.
Install matrix, hardware requirements, supported model families.

use_when: A layout needs real imagery - hero art, textures, avatars, empty-state illustrations - and stock photos will not fit.
You want image generation running locally with reproducible, versionable workflow graphs.
You are producing many variants of the same asset and need a pipeline rather than one-off prompting.
avoid_when: You need UI components or design guidance. This is an image-generation backend, not a UI toolkit - it is indexed for the asset half of building an interface.
You want a zero-setup image API. Running it locally needs a GPU; the official desktop app and hosted cloud remove that, but both are their own setup and, for the cloud, their own cost.
The output would ship where the GPL-3.0 license or an individual model’s terms are a problem. Model weights carry their own licenses, separate from ComfyUI’s.

baseline.description: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

notes: Category outlier. ComfyUI is indexed as a visual-asset generator that feeds interface work, not as a UI library. It is also the only GPL-3.0 source in the catalog - relevant if anyone considers embedding rather than calling it. Its partner nodes call closed-source models (Nano Banana, Seedance and others) that carry their own terms and per-use cost, unlike the open weights it runs locally.
